overview: 3...a6 is the main road of the Ruy Lopez (roughly two thirds to 90 per cent of Ruy games per the sources). It asks White's bishop an immediate question: Bxc6 (Exchange) or the retreat 4.Ba4, after which Black can play ...b5 to kick the bishop again. The main line is the Closed Ruy (5.O-O Be7 6.Re1 b5 7.Bb3 d6 8.c3 O-O 9.h3), a locked, slow centre where White builds the c3-d4 pawn duo and reroutes the knight Nb1-d2-f1-g3, and Black seeks queenside counterplay with ...c5/...c4 or ...Bb7 and ...Re8/...Bf8. Alternatives at move five or later include the Open Variation (5...Nxe4), the Arkhangelsk (5...b5), and Marshall Attack (8...d5), with Anti-Marshall systems used by White to dodge it. Play is typically slow positional manoeuvring (the 'Spanish torture': a small White edge pressed for forty moves) with very deep theory. It has been a main weapon of nearly every world champion.

white_ideas.idea: Build the c3-d4 centre after castling and Re1, supporting e4.
Spanish manoeuvre: Nb1-d2-f1-g3 reinforcing e4 and heading for the kingside.
Keep pressure on e5 and d6 with the Bb3 and Re1; apply long-term pressure rather than seek immediate material.
Avoid the Marshall with Anti-Marshall systems (8.a4 or 8.h3).
Alternatives: Exchange with 4.Bxc6 dxc6 for a better pawn structure and endgame; Anderssen 5.d3 and Tarrasch 5.Nc3 for quieter play.

black_ideas.idea: Kick the bishop with ...a6 then ...b5, gaining queenside space and the ...a6-b5-d6 chain.
Closed set-up with ...Be7, ...d6, ...O-O, then Chigorin (...Na5, ...c5), Breyer (...Nb8-d7) or Zaitsev (...Bb7, ...Re8) set-ups.
Open Variation 5...Nxe4 for active piece play and the ...d5 break.
Marshall Attack, a pawn sacrifice with ...d5 for a strong attack; considered so sound that White often avoids it.

typical_structures.structure: Closed Ruy Lopez: pawns on e4/d3 or c3 vs e5/d6 locked or in tension, White later plays d4; centre mostly closed with slow manoeuvring
Exchange Variation: White gets 4v3 kingside majority, Black has doubled c-pawns and bishop pair
Open Variation: after ...Nxe4 and d4 exd4 the centre opens and pieces become active

character.notes: Main Closed lines are slow and manoeuvring, rarely forcing early, and Black has few ways to lose quickly, but the root as a whole includes the Marshall and Open lines which are forcing. Described as a slow positional struggle ('Spanish torture') with deep theory rather than tactical fireworks.

gambit.notes: The root position has no gambit. The Marshall Attack sub-line is a Black pawn gambit (8...d5) and the Open Variation briefly leaves e4 pawn, but neither is the main line.

soundness.notes: Fully sound at every level; main weapon of nearly every world champion. Equal or very slight White edge with best play. Marshall Attack is described as 'so sound' White often sidesteps it.

structure.notes: Main line is the Closed Ruy: e4/e5 pawns stay, c3-d4 prepared, centre locked or in tension for a long time. Open and Exchange branches open the centre. The central pawn skeleton usually stays on early.

approach.notes: Not a set-up; a heavily theoretical main line played by world champions and elite players. Berlin (3...Nf6) is the preferred drawing weapon at the top, but the Morphy remains regularly played in top-level competition.

level.notes: Theory extends well beyond move thirty and most lines are deeply explored. The closed structures also demand a good understanding of piece manoeuvres (Nbd2-f1-g3, Black's counterplay timings). One source says it requires learners to master heavy theory but you need not memorise twenty moves to play well. Judged for Black as the defending side studying 3...a6 lines; for White the Closed Ruy is the same.

plan_phrases: bishop pair vs structure in the Exchange
kingside attack from a locked centre

description.claim: The Morphy Defense is the cornerstone of the Ruy Lopez, the most classical response.
description.note: Described as the main road and most prominent response; most Ruy games go this way.
It forces White to decide between Bxc6 and retreat.

description.claim: It initiates a deep, complex struggle for central control and initiative.
description.note: Deep theory and long-term strategic struggle; 'initiative' is less apt for the slow Closed lines but not wrong.

common_plans.claim: White: Execute the c3-d4 central push.
common_plans.note: Standard White plan in the Closed Ruy.
The standard manoeuvre is with the queen's knight, Nb1-d2-f1-g3, not Nf3-d2. The Nf3 stays on f3 to support d4.
Knight to g3, Nf5/h4 ideas; the 'Spanish torture' often meets with pressure on both wings.

common_plans.claim: Black: Prepare a queenside counter-attack with ...b5.
common_plans.note: ...b5 kicks the bishop and gains space; ...c5/...c4 follow.

No source names challenging White's bishop pair as a Black plan in the Morphy. In the Exchange Variation it is Black who has the bishop pair. Own understanding: Black's usual plan against the Bb3 is ...Na5 (Chigorin) to trade it off.
...d5 is the central break in the Open Variation and the Marshall (and the Berlin/Arkhangelsk lines).
